mainTopic: Vows made by comparison: "like the vows of the רשעים," "like the vows of the כשרים," and "like their נדבות", and which תנא splits a נדר from a נדבה
overview: The משנה teaches that saying "like the vows of the רשעים" counts as a vow of נזירות, קרבן, or שבועה. Saying "like the vows of the כשרים" means nothing, because good people do not make vows. Saying "like their נדבות" counts as נזירות or קרבן. The גמרא worries that "like the vows of the רשעים" might mean "I will NOT vow like them." שמואל answers that the person added a word: הריני (נזירות), עלי (קרבן), or הימנו (שבועה). The גמרא challenges הריני and הימנו. It answers that a נזיר was walking by, and that the person said "from it, that I will not eat." It also explains the חידוש: a שבועה works even without saying the word שבועה. Finally, the גמרא asks which תנא splits a נדר from a נדבה, since a ברייתא suggests that neither רבי מאיר nor רבי יהודה does. It begins to answer that the משנה can follow רבי מאיר, and the explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The משנה: vows of the wicked, of the virtuous, and their gift offerings
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists three phrases. It tells us which ones create a vow and what kind of vow each one creates.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone says "like the vows of the wicked," he has vowed to be a nazirite, to bring an offering, or to take an oath. If he says "like the vows of the virtuous," he has said nothing. If he says "like their gift offerings," he has vowed to be a nazirite or to bring an offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives three phrases a person might say. It rules on whether each one creates a vow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רשעים are the kind of people who make vows, so comparing yourself to them counts as a real vow. כשרים do not make vows, so comparing yourself to them adds nothing. כשרים do bring נדבות and become נזירים, so "like their נדבות" covers נזירות and קרבן, but not שבועה.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (the base text)
Wicked people
Virtuous, upright people
Gift offerings, given freely
A nazirite, someone who vows off wine, haircuts, and contact with the dead
An oath

steps.confusionAlert: "Like their נדבות" refers back to the כשרים, the good people. It does NOT refer to the רשעים. That is why it covers only נזירות and קרבן, the things good people do, and not שבועה.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
If he says "like the vows of the wicked":
he has vowed regarding being a nazirite, an offering, or an oath.
If he says "like the vows of the virtuous":
he has not said anything.
If he says "like their gift offerings":
phrases.notes: "Their" means the virtuous people just mentioned.

phrases.english: he has vowed regarding being a nazirite or an offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ כְּנִדְרֵי רְשָׁעִים נָדַר בְּנָזִיר וּבְקׇרְבָּן וּבִשְׁבוּעָה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: "Like the vows of the רשעים" creates נזירות, קרבן, or שבועה. "Like the vows of the כשרים" creates nothing. "Like their נדבות" creates נזירות or קרבן.

steps.title: Maybe he meant he will NOT vow like the wicked
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the first ruling of the משנה. The phrase "like the vows of the רשעים" could be a refusal to vow, not a vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: But perhaps this is what he is saying: "Like the vows of the wicked, I do not vow!"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions how the משנה can treat "like the vows of the רשעים" as a vow. The person might have meant the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words by themselves are unclear. They could mean "I take on a vow like the רשעים do" or "I am not going to vow like the רשעים." If the second meaning is possible, we should not obligate him.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that analyzes the משנה
But perhaps (opens a challenge)
This is what he is saying
I do not vow

phrases.english: Gemara:
But perhaps this is what he is saying:
"Like the vows of the wicked I do not vow"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first clause of the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that "like the vows of the רשעים" is a vow
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The phrase is unclear. It could be a refusal to vow rather than a vow.

steps.title: שמואל: he added a word that shows which vow he meant
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that the person added a key word after the phrase. That word makes it a clear vow and tells us which type.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: The case is one who said, "Like the vows of the wicked, I am hereby," or "upon me," or "from it." "I am hereby" means naziriteship. "Upon me" means an offering. "From it" means an oath.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the challenge. He says the משנה is talking about someone who added an extra word to his statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adding הריני, עלי, or הימנו shows that the person is taking something on, not refusing. Each word also matches a different vow: הריני is about the person himself (נזירות), עלי is an obligation on him (קרבן), and הימנו restricts him from something (שבועה).

keyTerms.meaning: An early אמורא in בבל
I am hereby
Upon me (I take on an obligation)
From it
The state of being a nazirite

steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of the sugya tests each of these three words one at a time.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
It is a case of one who says, "Like the vows of the wicked
I am hereby," or "upon me," or "from it."
"I am hereby" refers to naziriteship;
"upon me" refers to an offering;
"from it" refers to an oath.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל בְּאוֹמֵר כְּנִדְרֵי רְשָׁעִים הֲרֵינִי עָלַי וְהֵימֶנּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by narrowing the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase alone might be a refusal to vow.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is talking about someone who added הריני, עלי, or הימנו, which makes it a clear vow of a specific type.

steps.title: Maybe "I am hereby" means a fast, not naziriteship
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל's reading of הריני. It could mean taking on a fast instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: "I am hereby" means naziriteship? Perhaps he is saying "I am hereby in a fast"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first of שמואל's three words. Why must הריני mean נזירות?
steps.deeperAnalysis: "I am hereby" only says that the person is taking something on. It does not say what. A תענית is another possible meaning, so connecting הריני to נזירות seems unproven.

keyTerms.meaning: A fast
Perhaps

phrases.english: "I am hereby" means naziriteship?
Perhaps he is saying "I am hereby in a fast"?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵינִי נְזִירוּת דִּלְמָא הֲרֵינִי בְּתַעֲנִית קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first word in שמואל's answer
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's claim that הריני means נזירות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: הריני could just as easily mean taking on a תענית.

steps.title: שמואל: a nazirite was passing by
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers that a נזיר was walking past when the person spoke, so his words clearly point to נזירות.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: It is a case where a nazirite was passing in front of him.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל narrows the case. The setting makes it clear what the person meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Words alone are unclear, but the situation explains them. Because a נזיר was right there, "I am hereby" means "I am like him": a נזיר.

keyTerms.meaning: Passing in front of him

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
When a nazirite was passing in front of him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל כְּשֶׁהָיָה נָזִיר עוֹבֵר לְפָנָיו
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case through the setting
steps.terutzMaskana: A נזיר was passing by, so הריני clearly means נזירות.

steps.title: Maybe "from it" means he WILL eat from it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל's reading of הימנו. It could mean "I will eat from it," which is not an oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: ("Upon me" means an offering.) "From it" means an oath? Perhaps he is saying "from it I will eat"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts עלי as an offering and moves on to test הימנו. Why must it mean a שבועה of holding back?
steps.deeperAnalysis: "From it" does not say whether the person will eat or not eat. If he meant "I will eat from it," there is no restriction here at all.

keyTerms.meaning: That I will eat

phrases.english: ("Upon me" refers to an offering.)
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets. Either way, the גמרא has no question on עלי.

phrases.english: "From it" refers to an oath?
Perhaps he is saying "from it I will eat"!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵימֶנּוּ בִּשְׁבוּעָה דִּלְמָא הֵימֶנּוּ דְּאָכֵילְנָא קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the הריני discussion and challenges the third word in שמואל's answer
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's claim that הימנו means a שבועה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: "From it" could mean "I will eat from it," which restricts nothing.

steps.title: רבא: he said "from it, that I will not eat"
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the person explicitly said "from it, that I will not eat," which makes it a clear שבועה of holding back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is a case where he said, "From it, that I will not eat."
steps.whatsHappening: רבא narrows the case. The person spelled out that he will not eat, so it is clearly a restriction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the person says "that I will not eat," the unclear meaning is gone. Combined with "like the vows of the רשעים," this is a שבועה. With this answer, all three words in שמואל's explanation have been accepted or defended.

keyTerms.meaning: A leading אמורא in בבל
That I will not eat

steps.whatToRemember: "Like the vows of the רשעים" counts as a vow only when the person adds a word that shows what he is taking on. הריני means נזירות (when a נזיר is passing by), עלי means קרבן, and הימנו means שבועה (when he says "that I will not eat").

phrases.english: Rava said:
It is where he said, "From it, that I will not eat."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא דְּאָמַר הֵימֶנּוּ שֶׁלֹּא אוֹכַל
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case through explicit wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: הימנו might mean "I will eat from it."
steps.terutzMaskana: The person said "from it, that I will not eat," which is clearly a שבועה.

steps.title: If He Spelled It Out, What Is the חידוש?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what we learn from רבא's case if the person clearly said 'that I will not eat.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is the point of saying it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבא's answer from Step 7. If the person spelled out his meaning so clearly, why would anyone need to be told that it counts?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said the person said 'from it, that I will not eat.' That sounds so obvious that the ruling seems to teach nothing new. A ruling has to add something, so the גמרא asks what it adds here.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: if what you just said is true
What is there to say? This case is obvious.

phrases.english: If so, what is the point of saying it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the usefulness of רבא's answer in Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's explanation that the person said 'from it, that I will not eat'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the wording is that explicit, the ruling seems obvious and has no reason to be taught.

steps.title: We Might Think an Oath Needs the Word 'Oath'
steps.stepSummary: The חידוש is that it counts as a שבועה even though he never said the word שבועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: he did not say the word 'oath' with his mouth. So the ruling teaches us that this still counts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by showing what new thing the ruling teaches. We might have thought there is no oath because the person never said the word שבועה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person said 'that I will not eat' but never said 'I swear.' We could have thought an oath only takes effect when that word is spoken. The ruling teaches that a clear hint like this works even without it.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said: introduces the mistaken idea the ruling comes to reject
Brings out from his mouth: actually says it out loud
It teaches us: introduces the new point being taught

steps.whatToRemember: A יד for a שבועה, a clear partial phrase, works even if the word שבועה itself is never said.

phrases.english: You might have said:
but he did not bring out the word 'oath' from his mouth,
so it teaches us that this counts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 8 by naming the mistaken idea the ruling rules out.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies the hidden chiddush (מהו דתימא / קא משמע לן)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without saying the word שבועה, no oath takes effect.
steps.terutzMaskana: The clear phrase works as a שבועה even without the word itself.

steps.title: Which תנא Splits a Vow From a Gift Offering?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the כשרים and asks whose view it follows, suggesting it fits neither רבי מאיר nor רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Like the vows of the virtuous': he said nothing. 'Like their gift offerings': he has vowed. Who is the תנא who sees a difference between a vow and a gift offering? Shall we say it is neither רבי מאיר nor רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה. It asks which תנא holds that good people avoid a נדר but do bring a נדבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says 'like the vows of the כשרים' means nothing, because good people don't make vows. But 'like their נדבות' does work, because good people do bring נדבות. So the משנה treats a נדר and a נדבה differently, and the גמרא wants to know which תנא holds that.

keyTerms.meaning: A vow: here, promising an offering you take on yourself as a duty
A gift offering: setting aside a specific animal as a voluntary gift
Who is the תנא? Asks whose opinion a teaching follows
Shall we say? Floats a suggestion

phrases.english: 'Like the vows of the virtuous': he has not said anything,
'Like their gift offerings': he has vowed, etc.
phrases.notes: The rest of the משנה says he has taken on נזירות and an offering.

phrases.english: Who is the תנא for whom there is a difference
between a vow and a gift offering?

phrases.aramaic: לֵימָא לָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר וְלָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה!
phrases.english: Shall we say it is not רבי מאיר and not רבי יהודה!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן תַּנָּא דְּשָׁאנֵי לֵיהּ בֵּין נֶדֶר לִנְדָבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the next line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that good people avoid a נדר but bring a נדבה.

steps.title: The ברייתא: רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה on Vowing
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows רבי מאיר says it is best never to vow, and רבי יהודה says it is best to vow and pay. Neither one seems to split נדר from נדבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: 'Better that you should not vow' and so on. Better than both is one who does not vow at all: so says רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: better than both is one who vows and pays.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up its suggestion from Step 10. It shows that neither רבי מאיר nor רבי יהודה seems to fit the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק compares not vowing with vowing and not paying. רבי מאיר says the best choice of all is never to vow, and רבי יהודה says the best choice of all is to vow and pay. Neither one seems to separate a נדר from a נדבה, so neither seems to match a משנה that treats them differently.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
At all
Vows and pays: makes a vow and keeps it

steps.confusionAlert: 'Better than this and that' does not mean the same two people for both תנאים. רבי מאיר says never vowing beats both kinds of vowers. רבי יהודה says vowing and paying beats both never vowing and vowing without paying. Both agree vowing without paying is worst.

phrases.english: As it was taught: 'Better that you should not vow,' etc.
Better than this one and that one
phrases.notes: The other two people. For רבי מאיר, that's both kinds of vowers; for רבי יהודה, the one who never vows and the one who vows but doesn't pay.

phrases.english: is one who does not vow at all,
these are the words of רבי מאיר.
רבי יהודה says:
Better than this one and that one is one who vows and pays.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind Step 10's claim that neither תנא fits.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the משנה matches neither רבי מאיר nor רבי יהודה

steps.title: It Can Even Fit רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts its answer: the משנה can follow רבי מאיר after all.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say it follows רבי מאיר,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to answer the question from Step 10. This line only opens the answer, and the explanation of how רבי מאיר fits comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא rejects the idea that the משנה fits no one. It claims רבי מאיר's view can include a split between a נדר and a נדבה. The reason is still coming.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say: introduces an answer that fits the opinion we thought it didn't

phrases.english: You can even say it is רבי מאיר,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the answer to the question raised in Steps 10–11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Fits the משנה into רבי מאיר's view; the explanation follows
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה matches neither רבי מאיר nor רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה can follow רבי מאיר. The reason is given in the next lines.
